21.t: Working with data: light, carbon dioxide and pondweed
q: Identify the limiting factor at light intensity 10% for both curves. Explain.
Light: both curves give almost the same rate, and the rate rises as light rises.
Identify the limiting factor for the low-CO₂ curve at 80% light. Explain.
CO₂ concentration: the curve has levelled off, and more CO₂ (upper curve) raises the rate at the same light.
Calculate how many times faster the rate is with high CO₂ than with low CO₂ at 100% light.
Counting bubbles is not very accurate. Suggest two improvements to the method.

Any two: collect the gas volume in a syringe or capillary (bubbles vary in size); keep temperature constant with a water bath or heat filter; let the plant adjust to each light level first; repeat and take means.
A grower adds CO₂ to a glasshouse in weak winter light. Use the data to evaluate this decision.

At low light, light is limiting: extra CO₂ raised the rate only from 8 to 9 bubbles. Most of the money would be wasted. Adding light, or adding CO₂ only when light is strong, would give a bigger increase.
